beats.text: In 2021, one bad settings change made Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp vanish for about six hours. Now imagine the whole internet.
beats.dir: dramatic hook; single read, no repetition

beats.text: Meta said a faulty configuration change on its backbone routers cut its data centers off.
Even many of its own internal tools went down with it.
And most of the internet doesn't travel through space: over ninety-nine percent of data between continents runs through cables on the sea floor.
beats.dir: surprising reveal; single read, no repetition

beats.text: In 2024, three of those cables were cut in the Red Sea, most likely by a ship's dragging anchor.
beats.dir: storytelling, ominous; single read, no repetition

beats.text: The UN estimates about a quarter of data traffic between Europe and Asia was disrupted.
Lose all of it, and it's not just social media: card payments, maps, ride apps and online banking all stop working.
The internet isn't a cloud. It's cables, routers and settings, which is why engineers build so many backup routes.
beats.dir: satisfying payoff; single read, no repetition
